summary.intent: Complete Phase 23 (Rust SDK Extraction) gap closure, run a security review, add unit test coverage for the Rust crates, and get PR #352 merged by fixing CI failures and resolving all reviewer comments.
summary.outcome: Phase 23 was fully completed, 163 new Rust unit tests were added (168 total), two HIGH security findings were fixed, PR #352 was created and all 28 reviewer threads were resolved across three review rounds, though CI was still failing at session end with Windows cargo check and cross-language parity issues.

repo: fuser is a Unix-only vendored crate; it must be gated behind [target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies] in both crates/fuse/Cargo.toml and apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml to prevent compilation on Windows

apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml depends on cipherbox-fuse without default-features = false, which causes cipherbox-fuse's default 'fuse' feature (pulling in fuser) to activate transitively even when --no-default-features is passed at workspace level
The cross-language vector parity CI job fails because @cipherbox/core needs to be built before the TypeScript tests run; a 'pnpm build' step must precede the test step
1Password SSH agent is the commit signing mechanism and is intermittently unresponsive, requiring retries before succeeding
ed25519-dalek requires the 'zeroize' feature flag to be explicitly enabled in workspace Cargo.toml for SigningKey to zero memory on drop
generate_ed25519_keypair callers in write_ops.rs were wrapping the return in Zeroizing::new() redundantly, indicating the return type was plain Vec<u8> before this session

The cipherbox-fuse crate's fuse/winfsp features control which platform modules compile; crate-level ops files (operations.rs, read_ops.rs, write_ops.rs, dir_ops.rs) are gated on #[cfg(feature = 'fuse')]
IpnsPublishRequest derived Debug, leaking encrypted IPNS key material; fixed with custom Debug impl that redacts sensitive fields
api-client's get_bytes method was dead code (no callers) — removed rather than fixed
fetch_and_populate_folder and resolve_file_pointers_blocking were dead code in both macOS/Linux and Windows operations.rs — 181 lines removed

code.finding: generate_ed25519_keypair now returns Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> for the private key; callers in write_ops.rs no longer need to wrap in Zeroizing::new()

ipns_private_key returned from generate_ed25519_keypair is used in a spawned thread; Vec<u8>::try_into::<[u8;32]>() needed to be replaced with (*ipns_private_key).clone().try_into() after return type became Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>
Same try_into pattern needed the same fix on the Windows platform path
encode_libp2p_public_key was casting key.len() as u8 without validation, risking silent truncation; now validates that key is exactly 32 bytes and returns Result
IpnsPublishRequest needs custom Debug impl to redact encrypted_ipns_key and public_key fields
Temp dir cleanup was happening before unmount; reordered so cleanup always happens after successful unmount
Copy-paste bug: app_version field was being set to device_info.device_id instead of app_version; device_info fields needed to be saved before partial move into DeviceEntry struct
ed25519-dalek workspace dependency needed features = ['zeroize'] added to enable memory zeroing on drop
cipherbox-fuse dependency needs default-features = false to prevent fuse feature (and fuser) from activating transitively on Windows
Cross-language parity job needed pnpm version: 10 and a pnpm build step before running tests to ensure @cipherbox/core package is built

workflow: When an executor agent disconnects mid-plan, check git log to identify completed commits before resuming — avoids re-executing already-completed work
cargo llvm-cov --workspace is already configured in CI on Linux, so any new tests automatically contribute to Codecov coverage without CI changes
Three crate test agents can run in parallel (crypto, core, sdk) since they have no cross-dependencies during test writing
For [patch.crates-io] entries with Unix-only crates, moving the dependency to [target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies] prevents Cargo from resolving/compiling it on Windows
When Copilot/CodeRabbit post the same comment repeatedly across review rounds, it's appropriate to mark as 'not applicable' with clear reasoning after the first resolution
Pre-existing moved code (not modified in the PR) should be noted as 'not applicable' for review comments rather than refactoring out of scope

friction: 1Password SSH agent was intermittently unresponsive, causing commit signing failures requiring multiple retries
The executor subagent disconnected mid-execution with a ConnectionRefused API error, requiring manual resume and bookkeeping

Windows fuser issue required three separate debugging iterations: first fixing build.rs (insufficient), then gating with cfg(unix) target dependency (partially fixed), then also adding default-features = false to the desktop dependency
Cross-language parity CI failure root cause (missing pnpm build step) wasn't immediately obvious from CI logs
CodeRabbit re-raised the same ecies.rs min-size check comment across three consecutive review rounds despite being resolved each time
gh CLI log output for failed CI jobs was noisy and required multiple queries to extract actual compiler errors
open_items: CI was still failing at session end: Windows cargo check needs the default-features = false fix to propagate, and cross-language parity needs the pnpm build step — these fixes were committed but CI hadn't re-run to confirm
AES-CTR client-side integrity verification gap (HIGH finding from security review): client doesn't verify CID after fetching bytes, leaving bitflip vulnerability if relay serves tampered ciphertext

file_ipns_private_key in write_ops.rs uses ed25519_dalek directly (not generate_ed25519_keypair) and the private key bytes aren't wrapped in Zeroizing — noted as out of scope but is a related security gap
cipherbox-fuse and cipherbox-api-client have no integration tests — coverage improvements focused on unit tests only
Security review identified 4 medium and 5 low priority findings that were documented but not addressed in this session
